potentialIssues.description: Sidebar polls every 2.5s, but impulse loading and activity execution happen in real-time
potentialIssues.mitigation: Polling interval (2.5s) is acceptable for human monitoring. Users will see updates with maximum 2.5s latency, which matches the specification's 'real-time' definition (pseudo-real-time via polling).
potentialIssues.architecturalDecision: Current implementation uses polling instead of event-driven updates. True real-time would require WebSocket/SSE, which is documented as a future enhancement.

potentialIssues.description: SessionState.get() aggregates data from 9 sources. Potential for inconsistent state if updates happen during aggregation.
potentialIssues.mitigation: State aggregation is fast (10-180ms). File-based storage provides natural consistency within each read operation. Inconsistencies would be transient and resolved on next poll (2.5s later).
potentialIssues.evidence: Validation tests confirm state consistency across all test cases.

potentialIssues.description: If impulse loading or activity progress update during sidebar render, display might show stale data
potentialIssues.mitigation: Solid.js reactive rendering ensures UI updates when state changes. Polling ensures fresh data every 2.5s. Any stale data is corrected on next poll.
potentialIssues.evidence: Test Case 4 (Incremental Loading with Activity Progress) validates that both impulse loading and activity progress update correctly without race conditions.

conclusion.summary: sidebar-impulse-visibility is fully compatible with existing specifications (activity-state-transformation-tracking and impulse-usage-tracking). It acts as a read-only consumer of state produced by the tracking specifications, creating a clean producer/consumer architecture. No conflicting requirements or overlapping modifications detected. All validation tests pass. The specification completes the memory agent proof-of-concept by making impulse loading and activity progress visible to users in real-time.
